tagline: A long climb to the balds, and a longer wait for the road.
intro: From Tellico Plains the skyway leaves the Tellico River at about 900 feet and starts up into the Unicoi Mountains, through the Cherokee National Forest and over the line into the Nantahala, topping out above 5,400 feet before it comes down to Santeetlah Gap near Robbinsville. The two forests gave the road its name.
It was a while coming. In 1958 a wagon train of 67 covered wagons set out to make the case for it, and the road was dedicated in 1996.

moments.title: Haw Knob
moments.text: A 5,472-foot knob astride the state line near the top of the climb, reached on foot by the Benton MacKaye Trail.

moments.title: Hooper Bald
moments.text: A grassy summit at 5,429 feet that was once somebody's hunting preserve, stocked with buffalo, elk and wild boar. The boar stayed.

moments.title: Joyce Kilmer Memorial Forest
moments.text: From an overlook the road looks down on 3,800 acres of old-growth forest named for the poet of "Trees", with an easy two-mile trail looping through it.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook
